stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A straight rod carries current $I$ and sits inside a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$. The rod feels a force $\vec{F}$ — the Laplace force. Sweep all four sliders and watch how the force arrow (marked $\odot$, out of the page) grows or shrinks.
stages.concept: Laplace formula: $|\vec{F}| = B \cdot I \cdot \ell \cdot \sin(\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is the angle between the current direction and $\vec{B}$. When the rod is parallel to $\vec{B}$ ($\alpha = 0$) the force vanishes; the force is maximum when the rod is perpendicular ($\alpha = 90^{\circ}$).

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A target force magnitude $F^{\star}$ is shown as a dashed orange ring on the rod. Tune $I$, $\ell$, $B$, and $\alpha$ until your live teal force ring matches the target ring.
stages.concept: $F^{\star} = B \cdot I \cdot \ell \cdot \sin(\alpha)$. Many quadruples $(I, \ell, B, \alpha)$ satisfy this — the product $B \cdot I \cdot \ell \cdot \sin(\alpha)$ is what counts, not any single slider.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The field arrows and the force ring are hidden. Only the target value $F^{\star}$ is shown. Compute a valid $(I, \ell, B, \alpha)$ on paper, set the sliders, then submit. One try per target — a wrong submit rotates to a new target.
stages.concept: Inverse: fix $I$, $\ell$, $B$ at convenient values, then $\sin(\alpha) = \dfrac{F^{\star}}{B \cdot I \cdot \ell}$. Choose $I$, $\ell$, $B$ so that $B \cdot I \cdot \ell \ge F^{\star}$, otherwise no $\alpha$ works.

labels.tip1: sweep each slider across at least half its range
labels.tip2: match the live teal ring to the dashed orange target ring
labels.tip3: compute the quadruple on paper first, then set the sliders
labels.peek_tip_formula: Rearrange: sin(α) = F* / (B·I·ℓ). Pick I, ℓ, B first, then α = arcsin(F* / (B·I·ℓ)).
labels.peek_tip_anchor: Anchor: at α = 90° the force is maximal, F_max = B·I·ℓ. So make sure B·I·ℓ ≥ F*, then dial α down.

1.1: Try doubling I while keeping the other sliders fixed — the force ring should double.
1.2: Rotate α from 90° toward 0° — the force shrinks to zero even with large I, ℓ, B.
1.3: The product B·I·ℓ·sin(α) sets the force. Any of the four sliders can trade off against another.

2.1: Read the dashed orange ring's radius. Grow or shrink the teal ring until they overlap.
2.2: Fix three sliders at convenient round values (e.g. I=5A, ℓ=15cm, B=100mT), then tune α alone.
2.3: Inverse formula: sin(α) = F* / (B·I·ℓ). Pick I, ℓ, B so the ratio is between 0 and 1.

3.1: The force ring is hidden — you cannot tune by eye. Write out sin(α) = F* / (B·I·ℓ) on paper.
3.2: Pick large-ish I, ℓ, B so B·I·ℓ is comfortably above F*, then compute α = arcsin(F* / (B·I·ℓ)).
3.3: One try per target. Double-check unit chain: A × m × T = N. If B·I·ℓ < F*, no α exists — raise one of them.
